newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds end weak, reversing after U.S. March retail sales and PPI data send European debt markets running for cover.

The headline figures of a 0.1 percent fall in producer prices and a 0.2 percent rise in retail sales were both fairly benign, dealers said, but strong core PPI and an upward revision of February retail sales had been taken badly.
The data was another nudge towards the view the U.S. might raise interest rates again soon, they said.
Most of the selling was in futures though, one broker said, with cash flows still largely suspended.
"There was no cash selling at all even after the figures, prices were just getting marked down with the futures," he said.
Investors are seen still happy to sit on the sidelines in the current unsettled climate and likely to wait till the market is beaten down further before committing funds.
"If we get to yields of around 5.90 on the 10-year bond, then we may see some action from domestic investors," the broker said.
Another dealer said the negative tone in major bond markets was likely to spill over into next week and the Dutch market could stay under pressure.
"I don't think the U.S. is going to recover from its lows, so on Monday maybe we will see some more marking down here as well." -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
